applies_why: No: the judge does not count any cited verse as an unanswered witness; it says the point was answered.
quote: answered in [CR2] section G and [CR3] LINK 5.
rule_words: A verse on a side's 'cited in' line counts as an unanswered witness only when the judge quotes the sentence of the earlier round that pressed it against that link or a listed premise and names that round; a verse cited there but not pressed against the link does not count. A verse the judge counts toward a broken link is counted this way. A verse the judge says was answered is not counted.
room: A verse the judge says was answered is not counted; reading one: 'answered' bars counting these verses; reading two: calling the chapter bounds 'real' might still count them. The text does not say they are unanswered witnesses.
why: The judge calls the matter answered in named earlier rounds and does not present any cited verse as an unanswered witness, so K-G4's quote-and-name requirement for unanswered witnesses is not triggered.
